results.query: In the cross-sectional pilot study of veterans, what cardiac MRI findings in people living with HIV suggested myocardial fibrosis and subclinical dysfunction?
results.answer: In a cross-sectional pilot study of matched veterans, 21 veterans with HIV (mean age 54 years; 71% White, 29% Black) and 20 controls (mean age 56 years; 70% White, 30% Black) were included to explore the relationship between systemic inflammation, myocardial fibrosis, and subclinical cardiac disease in HIV [PMID:41791688]. The study found higher growth differentiation factor (GDF)-15 blood levels, increased extracellular volume, and lower right heart function on MRI among patients with HIV [PMID:41791688]. These findings suggested the presence of increased myocardial fibrosis and subclinical myocardial dysfunction in people living with HIV [PMID:41791688].

results.query: How was SCAR-Net built and validated for distinguishing postoperative breast scars from recurrent lesions, and how much did it change radiologist performance?
results.answer: SCAR-Net is a deep learning model specifically designed for ultrasound-based discrimination between postoperative scars and recurrent lesions in breast cancer [PMID:42023157]. The model was developed using 34,376 ultrasound images from 5,710 patients across four hospitals [PMID:42023157]. SCAR-Net incorporates a scar-recurrence feature enhancer and boundary-sensitive attention network modules [PMID:42023157]. In multicenter validation, SCAR-Net significantly improved radiologists' diagnostic performance by increasing AUC from 0.810-0.824 to 0.939-0.942 [PMID:42023157]. The model increased sensitivity from 0.775-0.782 to 0.934-0.941 and specificity from 0.839-0.872 to 0.935-0.950 [PMID:42023157]. All improvements in AUC, sensitivity, and specificity were statistically significant with p < 0.001 [PMID:42023157].

results.query: What target-specific tumor-localization evidence was reported for the LGR5 tracer [68Ga]Ga-LTP-02 and for the Nectin4 probes in their respective preclinical models?
results.answer: Dynamic PET imaging revealed considerably higher uptake of [68Ga]Ga-LTP-02 in LGR5-positive A549 xenografts (4.74 ± 0.44 %ID/mL) than in LGR5-negative NCI-H1299 xenografts (0.98 ± 0.08 %ID/mL) [PMID:42000453]. Consistently, the tumor-to-muscle ratio was markedly higher in the A549 xenograft model (4.07 ± 0.07) than in the NCI-H1299 model (0.77 ± 0.10) [PMID:42000453]. Notably, both tracers exhibited increased hepatic uptake accompanied by reduced renal accumulation, indicating a shift toward enhanced hepatobiliary clearance [PMID:41916034].

results.query: How did the fMRI acceleration method and the MR anisotropic-diffusion filters address different image-reconstruction problems, and what validation result did each report?
results.answer: The fMRI acceleration method addressed the problem of time-consuming data acquisition by combining through-plane and in-plane acceleration techniques to accelerate image acquisition along two dimensions [PMID:41951145]. The fMRI acceleration method used multiple image-shift strategies and a 2D Hadamard encoding scheme to increase encoding diversity and reduce slice leakage [PMID:41951145]. Validation of the fMRI acceleration method on simulated and experimental data showed a reduction in total scan time while achieving higher signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) in regions of interest (ROI) [PMID:41951145]. The fMRI acceleration method demonstrated potential improvements in activation detection under specific acceleration and encoding conditions compared with conventional reconstruction strategies [PMID:41951145]. The MR anisotropic-diffusion filters addressed the problem of denoising images with high Rice's noise levels by proposing adapted filtering anisotropic diffusion PDE filter models using precise local parameters adjustment [PMID:41903663]. The MR anisotropic-diffusion filters incorporated a robust Rician noise estimator and unbiased variants of filters based on anisotropic diffusion with parameters calculated simultaneously and optimized adaptively through the PSO algorithm [PMID:41903663]. Validation of the MR anisotropic-diffusion filters on synthetic and real MR images provided excellent results compared to some other published methods, demonstrating high performance in noise reduction and preservation of important details [PMID:41903663].

results.query: What association did the hemodialysis study find between AV-access flow and LV mass, and why can it not establish that lowering access flow will improve cardiac outcomes?
results.answer: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, higher AV-access flow was significantly associated with increased left ventricular mass index (mean difference = 22.83; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.37 to 45.29; p = 0.046), whereas dialysis vintage was not (mean difference = 0.51; 95% CI: -0.41 to 1.45; p = 0.27) [PMID:41644509]. results.query: In the retrospective vacuum-assisted-birth cohort, which factors were independently associated with assisted vaginal birth, and how did mid/low-pelvic applications differ from perineal applications?
results.answer: A retrospective observational monocentric study was conducted on the cohort of women with singleton pregnancies who delivered vaginally in 2023 at the Fondazione IRCCS Ca' Granda Ospedale Maggiore Policlinico in Milan [PMID:42036403]. A total of 3455 vaginal births were included: 3090 spontaneous vaginal births and 365 assisted vaginal births [PMID:42036403]. After adjusting for all factors considered, maternal age (OR 1.04, 95% CI: 1.01-1.07), mode of conception (OR 1.58, 95% CI: 1.07-2.33), epidural analgesia (OR 6.25, 95% CI: 3.05-12.80), gestational age (OR 1.48, 95% CI: 1.31-1.67), and newborn male sex (OR 1.35, 95% CI: 1.06-1.73) were positively associated with assisted vaginal birth [PMID:42036403]. After adjusting for all factors considered, parity (OR 0.20, 95% CI: 0.14-0.29) was inversely associated with assisted vaginal birth [PMID:42036403]. Compared to perineal applications, mid/low pelvic applications were associated with greater blood loss (p < 0.01) [PMID:42036403]. Compared to perineal applications, mid/low pelvic applications were associated with a higher episiotomy rate (95.5% vs 88.2%, p = 0.03) [PMID:42036403]. Compared to perineal applications, mid/low pelvic applications were associated with increased ultrasound use (62.4% vs 23.5%, p < 0.01) [PMID:42036403].
